### Second search icon FAB (symbol detail view) — `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/app/ref/index.tsx:346-353`

```tsx
>

```
(`onOpenSearch` is passed in from the parent at line 378 as `() => setSearchVisible(true)`.)

### The TextInput revealed by the icon — `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx:53-63`

```tsx
<TextInput
  ref={inputRef}
  value={query}
  onChangeText={setQuery}
  placeholder="Search symbols..."
  placeholderTextColor={colors.onSurfaceVariant}

  autoCapitalize="none"
  autoCorrect={false}

/>
```
There is also a decorative magnify icon at `SearchOverlay.tsx:52` inside the search bar:
```tsx
<MaterialCommunityIcons name="magnify" size={18} color={colors.onSurfaceVariant} />
```

## 3. How the icon and input are wired

State lives in the `Reference` parent component, not in the overlay:

- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/app/ref/index.tsx:363` — `const [searchVisible, setSearchVisible] = useState(false);`

The overlay is mounted unconditionally and just receives `visible`:
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/app/ref/index.tsx:465-469` (list view)
  ```tsx
  <SearchOverlay
    visible={searchVisible}
    onClose={() => setSearchVisible(false)}
    onSelectSymbol={handleSelectSymbol}
  />
  ```
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/app/ref/index.tsx:379-383` (detail view, identical wiring)

Inside `SearchOverlay`:
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx:18` — `const [query, setQuery] = useState("");`
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx:19` — `const inputRef = useRef<TextInput>(null);`  ← declared but never used to call `.focus()`
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx:40-44` — `handleClose` clears the query, dismisses the keyboard, and calls `onClose()`:
  ```tsx
  const handleClose = useCallback(() => {
    setQuery("");
    Keyboard.dismiss();
    onClose();
  }, [onClose]);
  ```
- `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx:47` — `<Modal visible={visible} transparent animationType="fade" onRequestClose={handleClose}>`

So the visibility flow is purely declarative: parent's `setSearchVisible(true)` → `SearchOverlay`'s `visible` prop flips → React Native `Modal` mounts its children.

## 4. Current behavior when the search icon is tapped

Tapping the FAB only calls `setSearchVisible(true)` (lines 458 and 378). It does **not** imperatively focus the input.

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  if (visible) inputRef.current?.focus();
}, [visible]);
```
(plus likely removing the static `autoFocus` prop, or guarding it).

Additional context: the same `setSearchVisible(true)` path is also reachable from the shake menu (`ref/index.tsx:394-397` and `:480-483`), so any focus fix in `SearchOverlay` would benefit both entry points.

Here's a complete report on the Word Wrap toggle crash. Read-only — no edits made.

## Summary of Findings

The previously-noted `lineWrapping` fix is solid and not the cause of the current crash. The crash comes from a different missing bundle export: **`DecorationSet`**. The generated bundle contains zero references to `DecorationSet` (not as a function, not as a value), so the line `var DecorationSet = _CM.DecorationSet;` resolves to `undefined`, and the very next use of it (`DecorationSet.create(...)`) throws a `TypeError`. The `setWordWrap` ON path triggers this because it destroys and recreates the `EditorView`, which runs the `p5FnPlugin` `ViewPlugin`'s constructor, which calls `computeP5Decos(view)` → `DecorationSet.create(...)`.

---

## 1) WebView-side `setWordWrap` handler + reconfigure logic

**File:** `/workspaces/learn-p5/src/utils/editor/exerciseHtml.ts`

The ext-relevant import alias for `lineWrapping` (lines 485) and `DecorationSet` (line 482):

```
478: var indentSelection = _CM.indentSelection;
479: var syntaxTree = _CM.syntaxTree;
480: var ViewPlugin = _CM.ViewPlugin;
481: var Decoration = _CM.Decoration;
482: var DecorationSet = _CM.DecorationSet;        // <-- undefined in bundle (see §4)
483: var autocompletion = _CM.autocompletion;
484: var CompletionContext = _CM.CompletionContext;
485: var lineWrapping = _CM.EditorView.lineWrapping;  // <-- previous fix; OK, see §3
486: var prettierLib = _CM.prettier;
...
490: var WORD_WRAP = ${wordWrap ?? false};
```

`getExtensions()` and the `WORD_WRAP && lineWrapping` guard (lines 608-626). Note the wrap extension push is an unprotected but truthy-guarded `exts.push(lineWrapping)`. There is **no Compartment/reconfigure** path here:

```
608: function getExtensions() {
609:   var exts = [
610:     basicSetup,
611:     javascript(),
612:     p5Theme,
613:     syntaxHighlighting(p5Highlight),
614:     p5FnPlugin,
615:     autocompletion({ override: [p5CompletionSource] }),
616:     keymap.of([{ key: 'Ctrl-s', run: function() { return true; } }, { key: 'Cmd-s', run: function() { return true; } }]),
617:     EditorView.updateListener.of(function(update) {
618:       if (update.docChanged) {
619:         postCodeChange(update.state.doc.toString());
620:         if (typeof window.__tutEdit === 'function') window.__tutEdit();
621:       }
622:     }),
623:   ];
624:   if (WORD_WRAP && lineWrapping) { exts.push(lineWrapping); }
625:   return exts;
626: }
```

The `setWordWrap` WebView message handler (lines 875-895). The reconfigure model is **destroy + new EditorView** (full recreation), not `Compartment.reconfigure`. The new view executes `P5FnPlugin(view)` → `computeP5Decos(view)` synchronously inside `new EditorView(...)`, so the crash happens during the `new EditorView` call below.

```
875:       case 'setWordWrap':
876:         if (view && msg.wordWrap !== WORD_WRAP) {
877:           WORD_WRAP = msg.wordWrap;
878:           var savedDoc = view.state.doc.toString();
879:           var savedSel = view.state.selection.main.head;
880:           view.destroy();
881:           view = new EditorView({
882:             state: EditorState.create({
883:               doc: savedDoc,
884:               extensions: getExtensions(),
```

content.text:
I have everything I need. Here is the comprehensive plan for all 8 features. (Plan mode — no edits yet.)

## Research findings that shaped the plan

- **Issue #5 root cause** is *not* the `lineWrapping` import (that earlier fix still holds). It's `var DecorationSet = _CM.DecorationSet;` (`exerciseHtml.ts:482`) resolving to `undefined` because `DecorationSet` is a TS-only type with no runtime export. `DecorationSet.create(...)` at `exerciseHtml.ts:545` throws `TypeError` exactly when the toggle's `view.destroy()` → `new EditorView()` runs `P5FnPlugin(view)` → `computeP5Decos(view)`. Fix: use the real runtime API `Decoration.set(decos)` (already exported via `_CM.Decoration`) + a `try/catch` guard around the recreation.
- **Issue #8 already wired**: `[id].tsx:567-582` has a 2-second long-press → `setSearchVisible(true)`. But `SearchOverlay` is always-mounted, so its `autoFocus` only fires on first mount — subsequent opens never raise the keyboard. That's the same root cause as Issue #4 — fixing the focus effect in `SearchOverlay.tsx` (add `useEffect(() => { if (visible) { setQuery(""); inputRef.current?.focus(); } }, [visible]);` and drop `autoFocus`) resolves both #4 and #8. Per your choice I'll also lower the threshold to ~600ms and add a light haptic.
- **Issue #7** — today `secondary` is a single `string`. Per your "Multi-alternate chooser" choice I'll extend the type to `secondary: string | string[]`, render a horizontal row of alternates in the popup with finger-follow selection (iOS-style), and keep `q→[1]`, `w→[2]` as single-element arrays so the popup is consistent.
- **Issue #6** — confirmed: in `QwertyKeyboard.tsx` the toggle is the *rightmost* button of the bottom row (lines 419–441), after hide-keyboard and space. Moving it to be the first child of that row is a localized JSX re-order.
- **Issue #3** — the symbol detail page (`src/app/ref/index.tsx`) uses a `FlatList` (no `ScrollView`), but the `ListHeaderComponent` mounts many child `<WebView scrollEnabled={false}>` instances (the live p5 example previews). Those WebViews hijack touch gestures even with `scrollEnabled={false}`, which is why the page won't scroll past them. Fix: add `nestedScrollEnabled` and route example-WebView touch events to the parent scroller, or convert the body to a `ScrollView` with `nestedScrollEnabled` on each example WebView. I'll go with converting `FlatList` → `ScrollView` with `nestedScrollEnabled` on example WebViews (cleaner and reliably scrollable).
- **Issue #1** — the Display Name block in `settings/index.tsx:302–320` reuses `card` + two stacked `cardRow`s, each with `paddingVertical: 14`, plus a divider. ~42px of padding alone, two rows of text. I'll collapse it into a single `cardRow` with label on the left and `TextInput` on the right (mirroring the Dark Mode row), removing the divider and one row's padding.
- **Issue #2** — per your choice (per-task if present, else exercise starter), the `setActiveTask` useEffect at `[id].tsx:610–627` will compute `const code = task.startingCode ?? state.startingCode` and pass `code` in the postMessage; the WebView `setActiveTask` handler at `exerciseHtml.ts:807–843` will accept an optional `msg.code` and dispatch `view.dispatch({changes:{from:0,to:view.state.doc.length, insert:msg.code}})` (same machinery as the existing `setCode` case at lines 800–806). The AsyncStorage draft save (lines 401–405) already keys on `state.code`, so saving `state.code` after the dispatch will pick up the new starter. No course-data changes required to ship — `shapes.ts` tasks simply fall back to the exercise template until I (or you) author per-task starters.

## Execution plan — 8 commits, one push at the end

| # | Feature | Files | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Display Name compact row** | `src/app/settings/index.tsx` | `v0.6.107` |
| 2 | **Reset editor on task change** | `src/app/learn/[course]/[id].tsx`, `src/utils/editor/exerciseHtml.ts` | `v0.6.108` |
| 3 | **Symbol popup scrollable** | `src/app/ref/index.tsx` | `v0.6.109` |
| 4 | **Search icon focus and raise keyboard** | `src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx` (also fixes the focus side of #8) | `v0.6.110` |
| 5 | **Word Wrap toggle crash** | `src/utils/editor/exerciseHtml.ts` | `v0.6.111` |
| 6 | **QWERTY symbol toggle to leftmost** | `src/components/QwertyKeyboard.tsx` | `v0.6.112` |
| 7 | **QWERTY multi-alternate long-press chooser** | `src/data/keyboardLayout.ts` (or inline `ROW1/2/3` in `QwertyKeyboard.tsx`), `src/components/QwertyKeyboard.tsx` | `v0.6.113` |
| 8 | **Run long-press search threshold + haptic** | `src/app/learn/[course]/[id].tsx` | `v0.6.114` |

Then one final `git push origin main && git push origin v0.6.107..v0.6.114` for all 8 tags.

## Feature-by-feature approach (brief)

**1 — Settings Display Name ergonomic.** In `settings/index.tsx:302–320`, replace the two-row card with a single `cardRow`: left side `flexChild`{`settingTitle "Display Name"`, `settingDescription "Used in greetings"`}; right side the existing `TextInput` (drop `borderBottomWidth`, give it `minWidth: 140`, `textAlign: "right"`). Remove the divider `<View>`. Result: ~one-third the vertical height.

**2 — Reset to next task's starter on task advance.** 
- (`exerciseHtml.ts:807–843`) In the `setActiveTask` handler, after the fade-out completes (or before the symbol re-binding), accept `msg.code` and dispatch `view.dispatch({changes:{from:0,to:view.state.doc.length, insert:msg.code}})` (guarded by `if (msg.code != null && view && msg.code !== view.state.doc.toString())`). Run the doc swap *inside* the fade-out's `animationend` so it lands during the opacity dip (no visible flash).
- (`[id].tsx:610–627`) Compute `const code = task.startingCode ?? state.startingCode` and include it in the `setActiveTask` postMessage. Also call `dispatch({type:"SET_CODE", code})` so React's `state.code` matches the editor and the draft-save effect persists the new starter.
- Run `npm run check-exercises` afterwards to confirm the validation rules still pass against the exercise-level `solution` (per AGENTS.md).

**3 — Symbol detail scrollable.** In `src/app/ref/index.tsx`: replace the `FlatList` body (lines 191–345) with a `ScrollView` wrapping the existing header JSX (the description/usage/symbols + examples block) and the prev/next nav. Set `nestedScrollEnabled={true}` on each example `<WebView>` (lines 242–250) so touch events route through the parent. Keep `scrollEnabled={false}` on the inner WebViews (they still don't scroll, but now the parent ScrollView does).

**4 — Search icon as input role + raise keyboard.** In `src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx`: drop `autoFocus` from the `TextInput`, add `import { useEffect } from "react"`, and `useEffect(() => { if (visible) { setQuery(""); inputRef.current?.focus(); } }, [visible]);` so every open raises the keyboard. Add `accessibilityRole="search"` to the input and `accessibilityLabel="Search p5 reference"`. On the reference screen, also wire the FAB's `onPress` to do nothing new (the overlay's focus effect handles the rest) — the *second* and later opens will now focus reliably, which is the user-visible bug behind "input role so it triggers the system keyboard."

**5 — Word Wrap toggle crash.** In `exerciseHtml.ts:545`, change `return DecorationSet.create(v.state, decos);` to `return Decoration.set(decos, true);` (the `Decoration.set` signature is `(deco: readonly Decoration[], sort?: boolean) → DecorationSet`). Remove the now-dead `var DecorationSet = _CM.DecorationSet;` at line 482. Also wrap the destroy+recreate block in `setWordWrap` (lines 880–888) in a `try { ... } catch (e) { console.warn(e); }` so a future unexpected plugin failure doesn't wedge the WebView. Regenerate `codemirror-bundle.generated.ts` *not* required (`Decoration.set` already works through `_CM.Decoration`, which is exported).

**6 — QWERTY symbol toggle to leftmost.** In `QwertyKeyboard.tsx:374–442` (the bottom-row container `<View style={styles.bottomRow}>`), move the `onToggleProgramming` Pressable block (currently lines 419–441) to be the **first** child, ahead of the hide-keyboard Pressable (currently 376–398) and the space bar (400–417). Pure JSX reorder; no style changes.

**7 — Multi-alternate long-press chooser.** 
- Change the `QwertyLetterKey` interface (line 19–23) so `secondary?: string \| string[]` (or introduce a new `alternates?: string[]` field — I'll keep `secondary` and widen it). Normalize to an array internally: `const alts = Array.isArray(key.secondary) ? key.secondary : key.secondary ? [key.secondary] : []`.
- Rewrite `renderPopup` (lines 166–202): show the primary glyph large, and a horizontal `ScrollView`-style strip of all alternates below; highlight the one under the finger (track `touchX` via `onTouchMove` on a full-width overlay above the keys, map to an index). On `onPressOut`, insert the highlighted alternate (or the primary if no alternate was selected).
- For the `q→1`/`w→2`/… cases that have a single secondary today, behavior stays the same (single alternate, auto-selected on long-press), preserving the existing fast path; for new keys I can later add multi-alternates like `a→[@]` becomes `a→["@", "&"]` etc. (no data authoring required to ship — current single-secondaries are wrapped in a 1-element array and the chooser just shows one glyph with auto-select).
- Add `LONG_PRESS_DELAY = 350` (slightly longer than today's 200ms) so the chooser has time to render before a quick press-release registers, plus a light haptic (`Vibration.vibrate(8)`) when the chooser appears.

**8 — Run long-press threshold + haptic.** On Issue #8: the `SearchOverlay` focus fix from #4 makes the keyboard reliably appear. Per your choice, also lower `[id].tsx:573`'s `2000`ms → `600`ms so the feature feels responsive, fire `Haptics.impactAsync(ImpactFeedbackStyle.Light)` (from `expo-haptics`) right after `setSearchVisible(true)`, and add `expo-haptics` to `package.json` deps if it isn't already (it's part of the expo SDK). Verify the short-press → `handleRun` path is unchanged.

## Verification after each feature

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — keep the count at the 2 pre-existing baseline (`StatusBarAccent.tsx` "hidden" + `[id].tsx:871` WebView overload).
- `npx eslint` on each changed file — 0 errors.
- `npm run check-exercises` after Feature #2 (per AGENTS.md — task validation rules may be sensitive to the `solution` field's relationship to `startingCode`).

## Commit + push plan

1. Bump to `0.6.107`, commit `v0.6.107: settings display-name compact row`, tag.
2. …through `0.6.114`.
3. After all 8 are committed and tagged locally, one final `git push origin main && git push origin v0.6.107 v0.6.108 v0.6.109 v0.6.110 v0.6.111 v0.6.112 v0.6.113 v0.6.114`. The `pre-push` hook will validate each tag/version pair (it checks the push range, so it'll accept the batched push because the bumped commit + tag are present).

A couple of small risks I'll watch for:
- **Feature #2 ↔ v0.6.104's task-progress toast**: the existing 480ms-deferred toast (`[id].tsx:454–456`) lands right after the M3 fade-through. Swapping the doc at fade-out's `animationend` (~158ms in) is well before that, so the toast won't race the doc swap. I'll keep the deferred toast.
- **Feature #7 ↔ v0.6.106's fade-through**: unrelated code paths, but I'll keep the keyboard long-press timers isolated in `QwertyKeyboard.tsx` (no shared refs with the editor transition).
- **Feature #3 ↔ #2**: both touch `exerciseHtml.ts`/`[id].tsx`-adjacent code, but Feature #3 is in `ref/index.tsx` — no conflict.

Ready to start executing on your go.
Proceed
